$comment: SOURCE REGISTER. Every row carries an official URL. 'verified' means the value was read directly off the linked official page by this session on verified_at. 'unverified' means no official source states it; the value column is left empty. Never infer or fill in a value.

sources.claim: Associates must clearly and prominently state 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'
sources.value: Required disclosure wording, Section 5 (Identifying Yourself as an Associate)
sources.note: Operating Agreement page shows 'Updated: October 15, 2025'. A violation of Section 5 is stated to be a material breach (Section 6).

sources.claim: Links must use the tagged Special Link formats Amazon provides; links must use the assigned Associates ID.
sources.value: Special Links required; tag must appear as a URL parameter (Participation Requirements, Section 2)
sources.note: Program Policies page shows 'Updated: April 14, 2026'. The supplied short links use the link.amazon shortener; whether that format counts as a compliant Special Link is not resolved by this page, which is why it is tracked as FLG-003 rather than asserted either way.

sources.claim: Associates may not use a link shortening service in a way that makes it unclear the visitor is linking to an Amazon Site.
sources.note: Directly relevant to short-link usage on a page. Our design therefore labels every outbound control with the destination Amazon listing.

sources.claim: Associates may not display customer reviews or star ratings unless obtained through Creators API or PA API.
sources.note: This is why no star rating or review excerpt appears anywhere on this site, even though ratings are visible on the listings.

sources.claim: Prices and availability may only be shown if Amazon serves them in the link, or if obtained via Creators API / PA API.
sources.note: Consequence: this site states no price. Prices observed on listings are volatile and were not API-sourced, so they are excluded rather than copied.

sources.claim: Associates may not engage in Prohibited Paid Search Placement, including bidding on 'amazon' or Amazon Marks.
sources.value: Commission Income Statement, Section 2(c) and Participation Requirements, Section 1(f)
sources.note: Sets a hard constraint on the paid-acquisition suggestions in the suggestion register.

sources.claim: Purchases referred by a link generated or displayed on a search engine are disqualified.
sources.note: Important nuance for the SEO plan: organic traffic must land on our own site, not on an Amazon link placed in a search result. Our design never places an Amazon link in a search result.

sources.claim: Purchases referred through a Redirecting Link (an intermediate site with no affirmative click) are disqualified.
sources.note: This is the reason the outbound counter is designed as a fire-and-forget beacon on a real user click, not an auto-redirect.

sources.claim: Associates may not cloak or obscure the URL of the site containing Special Links.
sources.note: Directly constrains any click-tracking redirect endpoint. Our endpoint is write-only telemetry and never performs the navigation.

sources.claim: A session begins at the click and ends after 24 hours, at order placement, or at another Associate's link click.
sources.note: Defines the attribution window the ledger's 'eligible sessions' column must respect.

sources.claim: Commission income is paid approximately 60 days after the end of the month in which it was earned.
sources.note: Sets the realistic lag before a campaign ledger row can show reported orders.

sources.claim: US payment minimums: 10 USD direct deposit, 10 USD gift card, 100 USD check, 15 USD check processing fee.
sources.note: Read from the Payment Minimum Chart table.

sources.claim: An Amazon Associates tag may not contain an Amazon trademark, and the tag must not be used in a domain name.
sources.note: The supplied tag shopnow047c-20 contains no Amazon mark, so this row passes. The site is hosted on github.io, which is not an Amazon-confusable domain.

sources.claim: The site must contain original content; third-party material needs significant commentary, analysis, or transformation.
sources.value: Participation Requirements, Section 1; strengthened by the April 14, 2026 update
sources.note: What's-changed page states 'Original Content Definition: Added definition requiring original content to contain commentary, analysis or transformation for additional value.'

sources.claim: From April 14, 2026 a 180-day limit applies: the product must be shipped/streamed/downloaded and paid for within 180 days of purchase.
sources.note: This is a forward-dated change notice on the official page. It is recorded as stated, not interpreted.

sources.claim: From April 14, 2026, products purchased by customers referred through any paid or boosted advertisement linking to Amazon are disqualified, with limited exceptions.
sources.note: Materially constrains any plan to buy traffic. Recorded as a decision input, not a recommendation to buy traffic.

sources.claim: Amazon's Commission Income Statement appendix links to a Standard Commission Income schedule.
sources.note: The schedule URL redirects to an Amazon sign-in page, so no commission rate could be read without an account. No commission percentage is stated anywhere on this site.

sources.claim: FTC: disclose a material connection clearly and prominently, hard to miss, with simple language such as 'advertisement', 'ad', or 'sponsored'.
sources.note: Guidance states disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT page, at the end of posts, or anywhere requiring a click. This is the basis for the masthead strip.

sources.claim: FTC: you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried, or make claims requiring proof the advertiser does not have.
sources.note: Governing constraint on guide copy: no hands-on test claims are made anywhere on this site, because this session did not test any product.

sources.claim: Google supports XML, RSS/Atom, and text sitemap formats, and recommends submitting a sitemap through Search Console.
sources.note: Basis for shipping both sitemap.xml and an RSS feed, and for the robots.txt Sitemap directive.

sources.claim: GitHub Pages publishes from a branch and folder, and can publish via a GitHub Actions workflow.
sources.value: Configuring a publishing source for your GitHub Pages site
sources.note: Basis for the Pages workflow in .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml.

sources.claim: An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) is a 10-character alphanumeric unique identifier assigned by Amazon for product identification.
sources.note: This is the 'checkable identifier' rationale for the product-intent record. Note the 10-character shape: the observed targets B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH and B0DZFD6R9Z are each 10 characters.

sources.claim: The five supplied short-link codes are not themselves valid ASINs in the form supplied.
sources.note: The codes B04G1MEwY and B02NbDxp3 are 9 characters, and all five use mixed case; an ASIN is 10 characters. A direct fetch of /dp/B0C8MOW59 returned no product. This does NOT establish that the short links are non-compliant — their compliance status is unresolved and tracked as FLG-003. Flagged rather than concluded.

sources.claim: Amazon Associates statement on influencer/advertising law: Influencer Content and Site are subject to Section 3(b) of the Participation Requirements relating to compliance with all applicable laws, for example the US FTC Endorsement Guides.
sources.note: Confirms the Operating Agreement and FTC guidance are cumulative, not alternatives. Both are enforced in the build gate.
